chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the Imam praying with four or five people, and two of them say that they prayed three (rak'at), and three say that they prayed four, and these say 'Stand' and those say 'Sit', and the Imam is inclined with one of the two or is equal in doubt; so what is obligatory upon him?

He said: There is no omission (sahw) upon the Imam if those behind him safeguard his omission with certainty, and there is no omission upon those behind the Imam if the Imam does not omit, and there is no double omission in an omission, and there is no omission in Maghrib and Fajr, nor in the first two rak'at of every prayer, nor in a voluntary prayer. So when those behind him differ from the Imam, then upon him and upon them, in precaution, is the repetition and taking by certainty.
ai.seo_question: What are the rules of prayer omission (sahw) for an Imam and congregation when they disagree on the number of rak'at?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the mechanics of 'sahw' (doubt/omission) in congregational prayer, emphasizing the Imam's reliance on the certainty of his followers to validate his actions. It establishes a reciprocal liability where the Imam is exempt if followers are certain of his state, and vice versa, with mutual doubt requiring precautionary re-prayer (i'adah). This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly principle that the validity of the Imam's prayer is intrinsically linked to the collective certainty of the congregation behind him.
